SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden‐onset dizziness/vertigo (“room is spinning”), constant for ~2 hours; associated ear “buzzing,” nausea, and unsteady gait.
- Onset & course: Began suddenly while making breakfast; continuous since. Similar self-limited episode one month ago (5–10 min).
- Negative ROS: No limb weakness, no ear pain/discharge, no recent viral illness, no fever noted, no hearing loss.
- Past medical history: Premature ovarian failure (on HRT).
- Medications:
  • Hormone replacement therapy – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Denies known drug or other allergies.
- Social history: Not discussed.

Objective:
- No vitals or physical examination performed (telehealth consult).
- No investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Vertigo
   - Assessment: Likely labyrinthitis.
   - Differential diagnosis: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), vestibular neuritis, Ménière’s disease.
   - Investigations planned: In-person assessment for otoscopic exam, blood pressure measurement, gait/neurological evaluation.
   - Treatment planned: Prescribed medication for symptomatic relief (drug name inaudible; 1 tablet PO three times daily × 10 days).
   - Referrals: Book face-to-face appointment with clinic physician; advise emergency department (A&E) if new limb weakness, severe headache, or intractable vomiting.

Quality checks:
● Missing/expected elements: vitals, full medication list/reconciliation (HRT details), social history (smoking/alcohol), drug name/dose for prescribed vertigo medication.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; medication name not audible.
